config_name: Gigabyte Gaming A16 — Core i7-13620H / RTX 5050, 24GB RAM, 1TB SSD

specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Laptop 8GB GDDR7 (~65-85W TGP)
specs.display_type: Matte IPS (retailer lists WUXGA; panel supplier varies)
specs.ports: 1x USB-C (PD, no Thunderbolt/USB4), 2x USB-A 3.0, 1x USB 2.0, HDMI, gigabit Ethernet, 3.5mm

battery.notes: 76Wh; lower-TGP 5050 slightly extends runtime vs 5070 tier (~6-7h light use).

price.notes: BBY API-verified 2026-11-24 (Black Friday window), SKU 20340722, reg $2,950.22. Marketplace seller — flag fulfillment/return-policy risk.

reviews.quote: Aside from the 8 GB issue, the GeForce RTX 5070 also achieved decent results, although sometimes you have to resort to DLSS or frame generation at higher details in its native QHD+ resolution.

praises: Cheapest current-gen Blackwell gaming laptop at BBY CA — RTX 5050 under $2,100 on sale
Same upgradeable chassis as the reviewed tier: 2x SO-DIMM, 2x M.2 (NBC)
Consistent sustained CPU/GPU performance (NBC pro on the platform)
180-degree hinge and decent battery life for a gaming laptop (NBC)
8GB GDDR7 VRAM matches the pricier 5070 tier
complaints: RTX 5050 is the weakest Blackwell part — a big gaming step down from the 5060/5070 tiers for little savings at full price
Retailer lists a WUXGA (1920x1200) panel on this tier — dimmer/lower-res than the NBC-tested WQXGA
Very loud fan under load (NBC platform con)
Screen bleeding and plastic chassis feel (NBC cons)
No Thunderbolt/USB4; marketplace seller adds return-policy risk

design_philosophy: The entry tier of Gigabyte's value-first Gaming A16 line: same plastic-but-solid 16-inch chassis and upgradeable interior as the reviewed model, with the money saved on the GPU (RTX 5050) and a lower-resolution WUXGA panel. It exists to undercut every other current-gen gaming laptop at Canadian big-box retail.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from NBC's Gaming A16 GA6H review (80%, i7-13620H/RTX 5070/WQXGA) with deltas: RTX 5050 vs 5070 -> gaming -2.0, creative_work -1.0, ai_ml -1.0; WUXGA 1200p panel per retailer -> screen_quality -1.0; lower GPU load -> battery +0.5, thermals +0.5. Panel specs (WUXGA) are retailer-stated, not review-verified. BBY per-SKU reviews unavailable — sentiment review-grounded synthesis.
standouts: Cheapest current-gen RTX gaming laptop at BBY CA ($2,050 sale)
dealbreakers: Weakest GPU in the line — the $70-more 5060 tier is far better for gaming
